title: No answer on the diagram
statement: Put no answer text on a picture or diagram.
detail: In one lesson build, the first diagram printed the rule and the role labels on the picture, which let a student pass every check without reading the passage. The course's authoring playbook now keeps a diagram neutral, showing only the labels its contract pins, and after authoring asks whether a student could pass every check from the diagram alone or from the prose alone; if either is yes, the lesson is below the bar. When a lesson's checks are meant to need both the picture and the text, make sure neither alone is enough to pass them.
against: A label that names what an element is, such as "habitat, not food", is part of the contract and stays; only a label that states the rule or a check's answer is forbidden (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/LESSON-AUTHORING-PLAYBOOK.md`, line 259).
